During the Iron Age, which began around 1200 BCE in the Middle East and southeastern Europe, iron largely replaced bronze as the primary material used for making tools and weapons.

Bronze is an alloy made from copper and tin and was the predominant material during the preceding Bronze Age. The transition to iron marked a significant technological advancement because iron was more widely available and could be more easily forged into stronger and more durable tools and weapons compared to bronze.

The adoption of iron tools and weapons facilitated advancements in agriculture, warfare, and various other aspects of life. This period of significant change is why the term "Iron Age" is used to describe this era.
